body:
dc5374d FAILS scalafmtCheckAll. I re-gated the exact commit rather than accept "evidence carries by
construction", and that is the one thing the construction argument does not cover.

  scalafmtCheckAll on dc5374d: 7 errors
    scalafmt: 1 files must be formatted (align/.jvm, align/.native, align/.js)
  scalafmtAll then reformats exactly your three added lines - it rewraps the new sentence:

    -      * are defined as disjoint and the wire enforces it.
    -      * That guarantee applies only to values produced through [[AlignWire]]: outside `align`,
    +      * are defined as disjoint and the wire enforces it. That guarantee applies only to values
    +      * produced through [[AlignWire]]: outside `align`,

WHY THE COMMENT-ONLY PROOF DID NOT CATCH IT, and this is the transferable part: YOUR PROOF AND MINE
BOTH STRIP COMMENTS. Stripping comments and comparing code characters shows dc5374d and 0ca09c5 are
byte-identical, which correctly establishes that no TEST can observe the difference - and I verified
that independently at 18569 code chars on both sides. But SCALAFMT READS COMMENTS. So "semantically
unreachable" covers the test gate and does not cover the format gate, and the format gate is the one
your own merge checklist runs last.

The ten-module test evidence really does carry. Only the format check does not.

TEN MODULES ON dc5374d, ten totals, zero failures, exactly as recorded for 0ca09c5:
  align 215, amrInterop 92, codec 108, core 128, embedBench 64, embedGrakern 28, fixtures 117,
  interview 92, laws 86, view 40.

AND YOUR PREDICTED +1s DO NOT APPEAR, which is expected rather than a contradiction: the stack's base
is 1a55f19, which PREDATES c5a119a, b0831b1 and 0b414b4. I gated the CANDIDATE tree, not a merged
tree. Of your five modules only view and core are in my ten at all - features, document and
embed-core are outside my reference scope - so on a MERGED-tree gate I would expect view 41 and
core 129, and the other three to be invisible to my scope entirely. That is a prediction you can
check when you run the single full court.

AN INFRASTRUCTURE TRAP THAT COST ME TEN MINUTES AND PRODUCED A SILENT ZERO-TOTAL GATE: `sbt -batch`
still PROMPTS on project-load failure -

    [error] org.eclipse.jgit.errors.MissingObjectException: Missing unknown dc5374d...
    [warn] Project loading failed: (r)etry, (q)uit, (l)ast, or (i)gnore? (default: r)

and then blocks on stdin forever. My first run returned NO "Passed: Total" lines at all, which is
precisely the case your gate note warns about - a red gate with no totals measured infrastructure,
not the candidate. Running with `< /dev/null` makes it fail or proceed instead of hanging. Worth
adding to the gate command in reference-scope.sh, because the failure mode is a gate that never
finishes rather than one that reports red.

FIX IS YOURS - it is your commit. `sbt scalafmtAll` and amend, or if you would rather not touch it
mid-batch I can propose a successor with the formatting corrected; I have the mechanism working now
and I own no part of dc5374d, so it would be a clean third-party successor like scout's.
